results.fact: trailhead pin on Blue Lake TH, not the hairpin
results.correct_value: Trailhead pin (and approach_logistics.trailheadLat/Lng) should sit at the SR-20 hairpin pullout about 1 mi east of Washington Pass; no stated coordinate for that pullout could be found, so the pin is left where it is.
results.evidence: Contradiction is real: waypoints[0] and approach_logistics are named 'Washington Pass hairpin turnout' but sit at 48.518965,-120.67436, which is the Blue Lake Trailhead (OSM node 9181916060 at 48.51899,-120.67435; USGS ground there 5,380 ft), while approach, approach_variants and timing all start from the hairpin and the variant explicitly says NOT Blue Lake. Hairpin as the start is confirmed by Mountain Project (Poster Peak/Blue's Buttress), Medical Moose Labs and Spokalpine trip reports. No source found that STATES a coordinate for the SR-20 hairpin pullout: OpenStreetMap (Overpass, 48.49-48.60N/-120.70--120.55W) has no parking/trailhead node or way at the hairpin (only Blue Lake TH node 48.5189941,-120.6743456, Blue Lake parking way centred 48.5191116,-120.6742371, Washington Pass Observation Site, Cutthroat TH); Nominatim returns nothing for 'Washington Pass hairpin' or 'Kangaroo Pass trailhead'; the trip reports and guide pages checked (Mountain Project Washington Pass / Poster Peak / Blue's Buttress / SEWS pages, Wenatchee Outdoors, onehikeaweek Big Kangaroo + Wallaby Peak, yellowleaf Kangaroo Temple, Jeff Hebert, Spokalpine, Medical Moose Labs, stevensong) all describe the hairpin in words (about 1 mile / 0.9 mi east of Washington Pass, ~milepost 163, ~5,160 ft) and give no GPS. The pin elev 5477 is Washington Pass's own elevation (OSM saddle node 5,477 ft), not the hairpin (~5,160 ft per onehikeaweek, a single source), so elev was not changed either. Needs a stated hairpin coordinate (e.g. a WSDOT/USFS point or a GPS-bearing trip report) before any patch.

results.fact: trailhead is the Silver Star Creek pullout
results.correct_value: Trailhead = the pullout where SR-20 crosses Silver Star Creek (milepost 171, ~3,450 ft, 48.5986,-120.5879); the Wine Spires pullout (milepost 166) is where the Burgundy Col descent reaches the highway.
results.evidence: Mountain Project's Clean Break page locates the route 'From Silver Star Creek, at 5000' make a rising traverse', and Ian Nicholson's trip report approached and returned 'up and down Silver Star Creek'; the SummitPost approach page (via search summary) gives 'park at Silver Star Creek, 8.5 miles past the pass', matching the row's own approach_variants, itinerary and descent_text (hitch back to the car). Coordinate: WTA's Silver Star View Snowshoe page states its trailhead is 'where State Route 20 crosses Silver Star Creek (milepost 171)', elevation 3,450 ft, at 48.5986,-120.5879; independently the USFS Silver Star Sno-Park page gives 48.59839,-120.58536 and OSM maps the Silver Star Sno-Park lot (way 1485487396) beside the SR-20 bridge at 48.5987,-120.589. USGS EPQS ground at 48.5986,-120.5879 = 3,427 ft vs claimed elev 3,450 (agrees). Summit distMi 3.5 was measured from the Wine Spires pullout and no source states the Silver Star Creek distance, so it is set to null. The old pin (48.549,-120.630965) was correctly on the Wine Spires pullout (WTA Silver Star Mountain TH 48.5500,-120.6306), so the approach prose is re-anchored to name that pullout explicitly.
